title: Affine diagonal conormal coordinates and normalization formula
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], let $C$ be its diagonal conormal [def-sc-diagonal-conormal], and let $U\subset X$, $V\subset S$ be affine opens with $U\subset f^{-1}V$. Put $A=\Gamma(X,U)$ and $R=\Gamma(S,V)$ with the induced ring map. There exists an $A$-linear equivalence $e:\Omega_{A/R}\to\Gamma(U,C)$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] such that for every relative derivation $D:\mathcal O_X\to C$ normalized as in [lem-sc-diagonal-conormal-derivation-exists], $e(\mathrm da)=D(a)$ for every $a\in A$. The equivalence is independent of the choice of normalized derivation and does not involve the sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$.

proof.text: Obtain a normalized derivation D₀ from exists_diagonalConormalDerivation. Apply the fixed-derivation affine calculation to D₀, giving an equivalence e and its formula on da.
For any normalized derivation D, the proved open-section uniqueness theorem gives D₀(a) = D(a). Rewrite the coordinate formula for e using this equality; the same e works for every D.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08S2: affine coordinate calculation for one normalized derivation; normalization independence proved directly using sectionwise kernels in the T2 second reading.

mathlib_searches.query: The sections of the diagonal conormal sheaf on an affine chart identify with the cotangent module of the kernel of multiplication, compatible with the normalized difference derivation
The diagonal conormal sheaf on an affine open is the multiplication ideal modulo its square, with normalized derivation sending a to the class of 1 tensor a minus a tensor 1
